svg.aria-label: The estimated 1RM and the records. The estimated 1RM of a ticked set, warm-up excluded, comes from two formulas: Epley, weight × (1 + reps / 30), and Brzycki, weight × 36 / (37 − reps). For 80 kg × 8, Epley gives 101.33 kg and Brzycki 99.31 kg; up to 10 reps their average is kept, 100.32 kg. For 60 kg × 12, beyond 10 reps, Brzycki (86.40 kg) is dropped and Epley alone gives 84.00 kg. At 1 rep, the 1RM is the weight itself. The records: each validated set is compared with what was done before the workout, and gets at most one medal, the highest. Gold, for a weight never lifted on the exercise; silver, for a better estimated 1RM without a record weight; bronze, for more reps than ever done at that weight or heavier. On the bench press, the previous workout had 80 kg × 8, 80 kg × 8 and 77.5 kg × 8. Today, after a 40 kg × 10 warm-up that does not count: 82.5 kg × 6 exceeds the heaviest weight of 80 kg, gold medal, +2.5 kg; 80 kg × 9 takes the estimated 1RM from 100.3 kg to 103.4 kg, silver medal; 75 kg × 10 does 10 reps where the best at 75 kg or heavier was 8, bronze medal; 80 kg × 8 equals what was already done, nothing. The exercise volume is 2,605 kg. Four rules: a single medal per set, the highest; you must do strictly better, and the estimated 1RM must gain more than 0.05 kg; the warm-up counts neither in the volume, nor in the 1RM, nor in the records; an exercise done for the first time beats no record, and with bodyweight only the highest rep count matters. The same rule applies during the workout, at the end, on the home screen and in the recaps; per workout and per exercise, one gold and one silver at most, one bronze per weight.
